subject: Packaging options for observability add-ons: retention, tracing, dashboards
messages:
From: Natalie Gomez <natalie@atlashealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability add-ons — sizing + pricing questions

Hi Maya,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our infra and observability teams as we evaluate Redwood for production: 

- Retention: we need span/log retention for 90 days for compliance with our analytics team, roughly 4–5 TB/day of trace ingestion initially (peaks up to ~7 TB/day).
- Tracing: we care about sampled traces + full-span search for P0 incidents; what's the pricing impact of index-on-write vs index-on-read?
- Advanced dashboards: our SREs want interactive dashboards (concurrent use ~10 engineers) with more frequent query SLAs. Is there a per-seat model or a seatless concurrency pricing?

Also, do you offer an introductory pilot with credits and a short-term discount for a 12-month commit? If you can send a short proposal and two packaging options (metered vs slab/flat), that would be super helpful.

-Natalie
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Health
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Gomez <natalie@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — sizing + pricing questions

Hi Natalie —

Quick summary and two packaging options attached (ops_addons_pricing_v1.pdf). High level: we can support the 90-day retention and the trace volumes you listed; the price swing depends on how much of the workload is index-on-write vs index-on-read and how much prefix/KV caching we can leverage in your traffic pattern.

Option A — Slab (flat) retention + dashboards
- Retention slab: 1 TB/day slab for X/month, next slabs at stepped price. 90-day retention packaged as 3x30-day slabs with a predictable monthly charge.
- Tracing: included sampling + 1x full-span search package; index-on-write enabled for a premium.
- Dashboards: seatless concurrent package (10 concurrent dashboards) at a fixed monthly fee.
- Intro: 20% discount for 12-month commit; 2-week pilot with $12k pilot credits.

Option B — Metered (ingestion + query)
- Pay-as-you-go per-GB ingestion and per-query compute for dashboards. Cheaper upfront for small usage, but variable.
- Tracing: pay-per-query index-on-read by default; index-on-write available as an add-on.
- Pilot: 60-day trial with $8k credits; first-month consumption proration available.

Attachment: ops_addons_pricing_v1.pdf (PDF, 28 KB)

Links: HubSpot deal HSP-9823: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9823

If it helps, Jordan can outline an alternate concession (ingestion cushion or extended pilot) depending on procurement needs. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Observability add-ons — internal pricing note

Maya — quick internal note on the two options before you lock in numbers with Atlas: 

- Index-on-write vs index-on-read: index-on-write increases cost by ~35% on our infra model given the sustained ingestion you quoted. For a long-term agreement we can offer a blended rate (index-on-write on critical services, index-on-read for lower-priority spans).
- Slab vs metered: slab gives predictability and is easier to sell to procurement. Metered helps them short-term but risks overage conversations later.
- Concession recommendation: instead of a straight 20% discount, offer a 12-month commit at 15% + 1-month waived for the first quarter OR keep 20% but limit to a 9-month initial commit. Also propose an ingestion cushion (first 10% of ingest free for 6 months) to smooth their ramp.

Attachment for proposal edits: SOW_AtlasHealth_draft.docx (DOCX, 45 KB)

If Atlas cares about dashboard latency SLAs we should clarify what 'frequent query SLAs' means and whether they'd accept a burst SLA backed by credits rather than contractual SLA at scale.

-Ben
Senior Sales Strategist
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Gomez <natalie@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — pricing options and pilot details

Hi Natalie — looping back with a slightly refined set of options after a quick internal review. I've highlighted the pieces below and attached the draft SOW for procurement.

Option 1 — Predictable (recommended for procurement)
- 12-month commit, slab-based retention covering 1 TB/day base with step slabs. 15% discount + first month waived.
- Tracing: index-on-write for critical services (blended pricing) + full-span search included for P0 access.
- Dashboards: seatless concurrency (10 concurrent users), fixed monthly fee.
- Ramp concession: 10% ingestion cushion for months 1–6.

Option 2 — Metered (recommended for short pilot)
- Pay per GB ingestion + per-query dashboard compute; 60-day pilot with $8k credits.
- Index-on-read default; index-on-write as a paid add-on.

Next steps: if procurement is happy with Option 1 we can issue a SOW and schedule a brief signature call; for Option 2 we can provision the pilot within 48 hours.

Attachment: SOW_AtlasHealth_draft.docx (DOCX, 45 KB)

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Monday to finalize?

Thanks,
Maya
From: Natalie Gomez <natalie@atlashealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — pricing options and pilot details

Thanks Maya. Procurement prefers Option 1 for budgeting predictability, but wants two clarifications before we move to SOW: 

1) Can the 10% ingestion cushion be applied as a monthly rolling buffer (so they don't lose unused cushion month-to-month)?
2) For the dashboards package: can we restrict the seatless concurrency to named users (we only have ~10 people who will ever use it concurrently) to avoid accidental spikes from scripts or automation?

If you can confirm those, we can get the SOW signed and aim for a Nov 1 start. Also confirm whether the 15% discount + first month waived is compatible with a PO-based procurement flow.

Best,
Natalie
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Gomez <natalie@atlashealth.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — pricing options and pilot details

Hi Natalie — quick answers to the procurement items: 

1) We can make the 10% ingestion cushion a rolling monthly buffer for the first 6 months; unused cushion will roll month-to-month within that 6-month window (not indefinitely).
2) We can tie concurrency to a named-user allowance (10 named users) with an override workflow if you need temporary increases — those overrides will be metered and billed at the agreed per-concurrency rate.

On the commercial flow: Redwood accepts PO-based procurement. We'll include standard PO terms in the SOW; the 15% discount + first month waived is compatible with PO payment under our legal team's review.

I'll get an updated SOW reflecting the rolling cushion and named-user concurrency in your drive link and loop in Kimberly for final billing code.

-Jordan
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
